operations.evidence: Canonical HEAD 76decba5609b67027edda750bb91519daa681ed6, UNCLAIMED ownership, existing continuation, pickup_requested queue and open H-to-F blocker were verified before writes.
A 15-minute lease was claimed only for official-source and line-by-line website evidence; runtime and business writes remained disabled.
The current accredited LSOA broad-age population edition was pinned to the 7 November 2025 release covering revised mid-2022 to mid-2024.
Population denominators must match the LSOA geography year and evidence period; no LSOA total was treated as a parcel population.
Accredited, in-development and supporting-information SAPE products were classified separately by geography and age detail.
SAPE was verified as the official between-census population source for Super Output Areas and related geographies.
The mid-2012 to mid-2020 backseries was identified as rebased onto Census 2021 LSOA and MSOA geographies.
The faulty OA lookup corrected on 12 March 2025 was recorded without incorrectly extending its impact to unaffected accredited LSOA and MSOA products.
SOA estimates use ratio change based on administrative population sources; they are modelled estimates rather than direct parcel enumerations.
LSOA estimates are constrained to MSOA estimates and MSOA estimates to local-authority estimates; hierarchy was retained in denominator interpretation.
Armed-forces, prisoner and usual-residence definitions were retained as denominator limitations rather than ignored.
The accredited LSOA density dataset was classified as contextual exposure information and not converted into crime probability or parcel safety.
CSEW was retained as national survey evidence with limited regional outputs, not as an LSOA or parcel source.
Interviewer-led domestic and sexual violence measures were kept separate from preferred self-completion measures because of under-reporting risk.
Incident rates, prevalence percentages, household denominators and personal denominators were recorded as distinct measures.
Any survey-table multiplication requires a population estimate for the same age, sex and population scope; mismatched denominators are rejected.
Calibration weighting adjusts for differential response by region, age and sex but was not represented as small-area representativeness.
Low unweighted bases, small police-area populations and disclosure constraints were retained as suppression and uncertainty gates.
Recorded crimes may later be transferred or cancelled under Home Office rules when recorded in error or contradicted by verifiable information.
Initial recorded counts were treated as mutable administrative records; area-level cancellation data were not linked to individual anonymised street records.
The availability endpoint was used to identify published street-crime months rather than assuming all historical months exist.
Stop-and-search availability is explicitly force-specific by month and was not inferred from street-crime availability.
The 64-character persistent_id was distinguished from the ordinary API id, which is not guaranteed stable and is not a police identifier.
outcome_status in crime-location responses was kept separate from the full dated outcome history returned by the specific-crime endpoint.
Location-id, point and polygon outcome queries all retain approximate-location semantics and cannot establish exact parcel attribution.
All 12 candidate rows remain unjoined with confidence zero because canonical F runtime, exact one-LSOA evidence and browser acceptance are absent.
Source rows 95-106 and operation rows 334-360 were prepared under the same continuation; the H-to-F blocker remains and no second runner, task, candidate value or business row was created.
